scheme_name: Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Support for Group Nurseries
description:
The Coffee Development Programme in the North Eastern Region is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to promote coffee cultivation in the northeastern states. 

This program was officially launched in 2000 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance coffee production in the northeastern states of India. 

The program aims to increase the area under coffee cultivation by 1 lakh hectares by the year 2025. 

It also seeks to improve the quality of coffee produced in this region. 

The initiative focuses on providing support for group nurseries to ensure the availability of quality planting material. 

The Coffee Development Programme is specifically designed to benefit small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers in the northeastern states are encouraged to form groups to establish nurseries. 

These group nurseries will provide high-quality coffee seedlings to farmers at subsidized rates. 

The government provides financial assistance of up to 50 percent of the cost incurred in establishing these nurseries. 

This financial assistance can go up to INR 1 lakh per group nursery. 

The program also aims to provide training to farmers on best practices in coffee cultivation. 

Training sessions are conducted by the Coffee Board of India. 

The Coffee Board has been instrumental in implementing this program effectively. 

Eligibility for participation in the Coffee Development Programme requires farmers to be residents of the northeastern states. 

Farmers must also be small or marginal landholders. 

The age limit for participation is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

Income criteria stipulate that farmers should have an annual income not exceeding INR 2 lakh. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Farmers must first form a group consisting of at least 5 members. 

The group must then submit an application to the local office of the Coffee Board. 

Required documents include identity proof, land ownership documents, and a group formation certificate. 

Once the application is submitted, the Coffee Board conducts an assessment of the proposal. 

If approved, the group receives financial assistance to establish the nursery. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the proposal. 

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the nursery. 

The Coffee Development Programme also includes a provision for regular monitoring and evaluation. 

The Coffee Board conducts periodic inspections to ensure compliance with the program guidelines. 

The program has shown promising results since its inception. 

As of 2023, over 1,000 group nurseries have been established under this initiative. 

These nurseries have collectively produced over 5 million coffee seedlings. 

The program has contributed to a significant increase in coffee production in the northeastern states. 

Coffee production in this region has increased by approximately 30 percent since the program began. 

The Coffee Development Programme also focuses on promoting sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farmers are trained in organic farming techniques to enhance soil health. 

The program encourages the use of bio-fertilizers and organic pest control methods. 

This approach not only improves coffee quality but also benefits the environment. 

The Coffee Board also collaborates with various research institutions. 

These collaborations aim to develop new coffee varieties that are resistant to diseases. 

The program has a strong emphasis on women’s empowerment. 

Women are encouraged to participate in group formations and nursery management. 

Special training programs are organized for women farmers. 

The Coffee Development Programme also aims to enhance the livelihoods of farmers. 

By increasing coffee production, farmers can earn higher incomes. 

The program has the potential to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is estimated that the program could generate around 10,000 jobs in the coffee sector by 2025. 

The Coffee Development Programme is aligned with the National Coffee Policy. 

This policy aims to make India one of the top coffee producers in the world. 

The northeastern region has a unique advantage due to its climatic conditions. 

The region's altitude and rainfall patterns are conducive to coffee cultivation. 

The program also promotes intercropping with other crops. 

This practice helps in diversifying farmers' income sources. 

The Coffee Board provides technical support to farmers throughout the cultivation process. 

Farmers receive guidance on planting, pruning, and harvesting techniques. 

The program also includes post-harvest management training. 

This training ensures that farmers can process their coffee beans effectively. 

The Coffee Development Programme has received positive feedback from farmers. 

Many farmers have reported increased yields and improved quality of coffee. 

The program has also fostered a sense of community among farmers. 

Group formations have led to better knowledge sharing and collaboration. 

The Coffee Board continues to promote the program through various outreach initiatives. 

Workshops and seminars are regularly conducted to raise awareness. 

The program is expected to expand further in the coming years. 

The government is committed to investing more resources into coffee development. 

This initiative is part of a broader strategy to boost agricultural productivity in the northeastern region. 

The Coffee Development Programme is a crucial step towards achieving self-sufficiency in coffee production. 

It aims to transform the northeastern states into a significant coffee-producing hub in India. 

The program not only supports farmers but also contributes to the overall economic development of the region. 

By 2025, the government aims to increase coffee exports from the northeastern states significantly. 

The Coffee Development Programme is a vital component of India's agricultural policy. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting farmers and promoting sustainable agriculture. 

The program's success will depend on continued support from the government and active participation from farmers. 

Through this initiative, the northeastern region is poised to become a leader in coffee cultivation.
